subject: house spider
title: 111,000 Spiders Share the World's Biggest Web and Don't Eat Each Other

scenes.text: These spiders should eat each other. They share one web.
It's in a pitch-black sulfur cave on the border of Albania and Greece.
The web covers over a thousand square feet, and holds about one hundred eleven thousand spiders.
Normally, the bigger house spider would hunt the smaller species living beside it.
But in total darkness, they can barely see. So both feast on midges that hatch from the cave's sulfur pools.
The world's biggest web has one rule. Spiders are off the menu.

description:
The largest known spider web lines a wall of Sulfur Cave on the Albania-Greece border: about 106 square meters, home to roughly 69,000 barn funnel weavers and 42,000 smaller Prinerigone vagans.
Both normally solitary species feed on midges that live off sulfur-eating microbes, and in the dark the bigger spiders seem not to hunt the smaller ones.
Would you walk into that cave?
first_comment: About 69,000 of them are barn funnel weavers, the same species that lives in sheds and houses. Would you keep this a secret or visit?
